newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Majority of Austrians wants EMU referendum -poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Austrians wants EMU referendum -poll.

text.p: A majority of Austrians wants the planned introduction of Europe's single currency to be put to a referendum, a survey published by weekly current affairs magazine News on Wednesday showed.
Fifty eight percent of Austrians say European monetary union (EMU) should be put to a vote, while 37 percent say such a step would not be necessary.

In a referendum, 45 percent of Austrians would vote against the single currency, while 34 percent would be in favour. Some 14 percent of Austrians would abstain from the referendum, the poll conducted by research institute Gallup showed.

The Austrian government has repeatedly rejected opposition demands for a referendum on the single currency and says it is convinced the country will be among the first wave of nations to join EMU when it is launched in 1999.

A survey published last month showed Austrian dissatisfaction with the European Union running at an all-time high at 64 percent. The poll also said that every second Austrian was against the single currency. REUTER
